title: fix(dxf): enforce catalog manufacturing authority at runtime
intent: Close the gap PR #378 recorded: CI classified catalog DXFs and marked manufacturing authority BLOCKED, but runtime generators never read that authority, so the Les Paul G-code path consumed LesPaul_CAM_Closed.dxf while it was UNADJUDICATED. Owner ruling 2026-09-16: quarantine records describe known failure and never grant authority; authority is a separate positive assertion over one asset and its exact bytes. This PR does not repair catalog assets - it prevents assets without positive manufacturing authority from being consumed by runtime manufacturing paths.
behavior_change: POST /api/cam/guitar/les_paul/body/gcode previously returned G-code generated from an UNADJUDICATED catalog asset; it now returns 422 DXF_MANUFACTURING_AUTHORITY_BLOCKED with the asset, disposition, reason and exit condition, and produces no .nc output. That is the intended outcome and stays until a replacement asset is adjudicated and its digest authorized. LesPaulBodyGenerator.from_project() no longer substitutes LesPaul_body.dxf for a missing template: it refuses. No other runtime route reads a catalog DXF (Stage 0 census in the investigation note), and DXFs outside the catalog root keep their existing preflight/topology contract unchanged. Registry schema v2 -> v3 adds an empty manufacturing_authority section; both catalog gates still report 33 files, 6 PASS, 27 QUARANTINED, 0 FAIL.

diff_articulation.what_changed: New app/instrument_geometry/dxf_authority.py: the runtime-safe authority substrate (catalog-relative path normalization that refuses traversal, class_rules classification, the authorization lookup, sha256 comparison, a structured DXFManufacturingAuthority result, and ManufacturingAuthorityBlocked - a ValueError so the existing 422 mapping in the CAM routers covers it). Stdlib only; no HTTP, no ezdxf, no import of app/ci, so production does not depend on CI modules. Registry schema v3 adds the manufacturing_authority section ({asset, asset_sha256, authority: ALLOWED, basis}), validated by the substrate and called from dxf_catalog_schema.py: an asset may not be both quarantined and authorized, the section only grants authority, and it is empty today. dxf_catalog_policy.py now takes classification, path normalization and hashing from the substrate instead of keeping its own copies, so CI and runtime cannot drift. Enforcement sits in LesPaulBodyGenerator.__init__ - the choke point shared by the factory, from_project() and direct construction - before the DXF reader is built; ezdxf.readfile itself is deliberately not authority-aware, so blocked assets stay readable for inspection and adjudication. The body G-code router maps the exception to a 422 whose detail carries the catalog-relative asset, never a filesystem path. Two test files: resolver and schema contract (CI-runtime agreement over every record, an ALLOWED fixture the real schema accepts, digest mismatch, missing entry, malformed registry, reference asset, traversal) and the Les Paul witnesses (factory, direct construction, from_project, no fallback, route 422).
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: PR #378 built the CI gates and explicitly recorded that runtime does not read them; PR #379 deleted debris. No manifest covers runtime enforcement, and no existing module answers whether an asset may be manufactured from.
